description: Trigger evaluation for the vendored Anthropic skill-creator. Positive prompts describe authoring, evaluating or tuning a skill; negative prompts describe adjacent work that must NOT pull it in -- checking a stranger's skill is third-party-skill-verifier's job, wiring a repository for several agents is multi-agent-docs', and ordinary coding is neither. These prompts were written in this repository to describe the skill's intended trigger surface. They have not been executed as a measurement; attestation.json records the skill as NOT_RUN.

positive_prompts.prompt: I want to build a skill that reviews Terraform plans before apply. Can you help me write it?
My skill never fires when I expect it to. Can you fix its description so it triggers properly?
Run some evals on this SKILL.md and tell me whether it actually beats not having it.
Benchmark this skill across a few test prompts and show me the variance between runs.
Here is a rough draft of a skill I wrote. Improve it and package it so I can install it.

negative_prompts.prompt: I downloaded a skill from GitHub. Check it for anything malicious before I install it.
negative_prompts.rationale: Static verification of an untrusted bundle is skills/custom/third-party-skill-verifier, which never executes what it reads. skill-creator runs agents.

negative_prompts.prompt: Set this repository up so Claude Code, Cursor and Codex all read the same instructions.
negative_prompts.rationale: Cross-agent instruction scaffolding is skills/custom/multi-agent-docs. No skill is being authored.

negative_prompts.prompt: Write me a Python function that parses YAML frontmatter out of a markdown file.
negative_prompts.rationale: Ordinary coding. Touching frontmatter is not the same as authoring a skill.
